facts.text: The project is a Python module for controlling the Tecan Genesis RSP 200
The module opens /dev/ttyUSB0 at 9600 baud with a 1 s read timeout and a 5 s write timeout; the portmon dump above it shows 8 data bits, no parity and one stop bit
A command frame is STX (0x02), the sequence letter, the unit address, the ASCII command, ETX (0x03), the XOR of those bytes, and a trailing newline
The sequence letters rotate through A-G
do_cmd reads a first acknowledgement and then a second acknowledgement/data frame
read consumes the byte after ETX as the XOR and does not compare it before returning a frame
Cmd_delayed stores (command, unit) pairs in cmdStack and start sends GFC, every stacked command and then GSC to the M1 controller
add_cmd appends to cmdStack and increments the class counter cmdCount
The logged write 02 41 4D 31 52 46 56 30 03 4E is STX A M1 RFV0 ETX and the XOR 0x4E
PAZ moves all installed tips to absolute Z positions in 0.1 mm; the range is set by the SRA command
The ROMA home action sends PAZ2480, PAR0, PAY0 and PAX0 to the R1 unit
The initialization sequence sends PIS to the M1 controller and PIA to the R1 arm
The dispense example sends V3600c900D217M0R to each of the diluter units D1 through D8
Cmd_delayed defines only __init__, add_cmd and start (lines 57-108), and the module's only close() closes the serial port (lines 201-203); no stop, abort, halt or emergency command exists

operator_required.reason: no text of the clone states the Z travel range: the PAZ doc block says the range is set by the SRA command (bin/tecan:243), which is a per-instrument setting, so the site supplies the range

safe_state.description: unreachable through this library: the clone defines no stop, abort, halt or emergency command, and close() only closes the serial port, so a latched e-stop cannot stop a move in flight
